clues.label: Born
clues.value: Born in Athens in the summer of 1961.

clues.label: Arrived from
clues.value: Joined the club in 1984 from Panionios.

clues.label: Country
clues.value: Won 78 caps for Greece, scoring 22 goals.

clues.label: Detour
clues.value: Spent two seasons at AEK Athens in the mid-1990s before a brief return.

clues.label: Club record
clues.value: Scored 125 goals in 252 appearances in his first spell, 1984 to 1994.

mysteries.notes: Wikipedia and GreeceIndex agree on all five clues.

clues.label: Born
clues.value: Born in January 1942 in Ampelokipoi, Athens.

clues.label: Wembley
clues.value: Captain of the side that reached the 1971 European Cup final.

clues.label: Country
clues.value: Won 50 caps for Greece and scored 4 times.

clues.label: Rivals
clues.value: Moved to AEK Athens late in his career and won a league title there.

clues.label: Recognition
clues.value: Received Ballon d'Or votes in 1971.

mysteries.notes: Wikipedia and To Vima agree on every clue; nickname deliberately excluded.

clues.label: Born
clues.value: Born in Katowice.

clues.label: Previous club
clues.value: Came to Athens from Ruch Chorzów.

clues.label: Golden boots
clues.value: Finished as the Greek league's top scorer three times.

clues.label: Amsterdam
clues.value: Scored in the 1996 semi-final win that ended Ajax's long unbeaten home record in Europe.

clues.label: Farewell
clues.value: Retired as a player in 2004.

mysteries.notes: Each clue agreed by Wikipedia and UEFA or Meczyki; goal totals and transfer year differ between sources so omitted.

clues.label: Country
clues.value: Cyprus's all-time leading scorer, with 32 international goals.

clues.label: Beginnings
clues.value: Started his senior career at Paralimni.

clues.label: Record move
clues.value: Signed from Iraklis in 2001 for a Greek record fee.

clues.label: Crossed over
clues.value: Later played for Olympiacos.

clues.label: Final years
clues.value: Won the Cypriot league with Omonia and retired in January 2014.

mysteries.notes: Wikipedia and UEFA agree; caps total and fee amount differ so omitted.

clues.label: Europe
clues.value: Top scorer of the 1970/71 European Cup with 10 goals.

clues.label: Height
clues.value: Stood 1.87 metres tall.

clues.label: Country
clues.value: Scored 6 goals in 21 internationals for Greece.

clues.label: Golden boots
clues.value: Greek league top scorer in 1970 and every year from 1972 to 1975.

clues.label: Record season
clues.value: Netted 39 league goals in 1971/72.

mysteries.notes: Wikipedia and UEFA agree on every clue; nickname excluded.

clues.label: Born
clues.value: Born in Santo Tomé, Argentina.

clues.label: Early career
clues.value: Played for Newell's Old Boys and Boca Juniors before Greece.

clues.label: Arrived
clues.value: Joined the club in 1979.

clues.label: Dugout
clues.value: Later coached the club to back-to-back league titles in 1995 and 1996.

clues.label: Europe as coach
clues.value: Led the team to the 1996 Champions League semi-final.

skipped.why: footballkitarchive.com reachable but its design text mirrors footyheadlines.com (same kit-news network), so no independent second publisher for design; Wikipedia only gives manufacturers; colours-of-football 404.
Only UEFA described build-ups (Warzycha in Amsterdam 1996 after Donis's run; Basinas penalty v Barcelona 2002); no second publisher describing the same move.
RSSSF gives XIs for 1982, 1984, 1989 and 2004 cup finals, but Wikipedia final pages render line-ups as images and worldfootball/11v11/transfermarkt blocked by robots or proxy.
